competences: The learner identifies key facts about members of the district council.
The learner explains the roles of district leaders using the sourced local-government materials.
languageCompetence: Learners read, write and pronounce: leader, councillor, district, local government, speaker, civic and political.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to consolidate the names and functions of councillors and local council officers.
By the end of the lesson learners should be able to answer original source questions about district leadership.
priorKnowledge: Learners identified the district council members and their duties in the previous lesson.
materials: P4 SST school reference notes on district leadership
references: P4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the preceding lesson on district leadership and asks "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee.". They use the pupils' answers to connect earlier material to members of the district council — part b.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous Social Studies period, answer the opening question and identify leaders within their local council.

steps.content: The district council has elected councillors. The district chairperson heads the district politically. The council includes a speaker and deputy speaker. The council has a vice chairperson. The council includes youth representatives. People with disabilities have representatives. Councillors represent divisions and sub-counties. The speaker chairs council meetings.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Remember the district council", including "The district council has elected councillors. The district chairperson heads the district politically." They explain the roles and ask "How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?" to check learners' understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read and copy the points, compare examples of district leadership and answer the teacher's questions about duties and positions.

steps.content: State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee. | How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community? | How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee? | Give any three ways leaders are important in the society.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original sourced questions, beginning with "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee." and "How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?". They supervise learners' written responses and check their answers against the leadership notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise independently, consult the facts in their notes and correct inaccurate answers after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher evaluates learning using "How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?" and "Give any three ways leaders are important in the society.". They recap the source-grounded points and assign the remaining revision question for later practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give oral answers, state one important district-leadership duty and correct their work in their books.

assessment: Check written and oral responses to "State any one role performed by the chairperson on the LC I executive committee.", "How is the LCI vice chairperson useful to children in your community?", and "How is the Secretary for defense useful on the Local council I committee?" and mark against the source material.
homework: Complete the sourced question "Give any three ways leaders are important in the society." in the Social Studies book.
